claim: Athena workgroups separate workloads, control team access, enforce configuration, and track query metrics and costs.
question: What are Athena workgroups used for?

values.display: separate workloads, control team access, enforce configuration
track query metrics and control costs

evidence.quote: You can use Athena workgroups to separate workloads, control team access, enforce configuration, and track query metrics and control costs.

claim: You can use workgroups to separate workloads, for example one workgroup for automated scheduled applications such as report generation and another for ad-hoc use by analysts.
question: How can workgroups separate scheduled reports from ad-hoc analyst queries?

values.display: one for automated scheduled applications, such as report generation
another for ad-hoc usage by analysts

evidence.quote: You can use workgroups to separate workloads. For example, you can create two independent workgroups, one for automated scheduled applications, such as report generation, and another for ad-hoc usage by analysts.

claim: Workgroups act as IAM resources, so resource-level identity-based policies control who can access a workgroup and run queries. A separate workgroup per team isolates queries, and each has its own query history and saved queries.
question: How do you isolate the queries of two teams in Athena?

values.display: workgroups act as IAM resources
its own query history and a list of saved queries

evidence.quote: Because workgroups act as IAM resources, you can use resource-level identity-based policies to control who can access a workgroup and run queries in it. To isolate queries for two different teams in your organization, you can create a separate workgroup for each team. Each workgroup has its own query history and a list of saved queries for the queries in that workgroup, and not for all queries in the account.

claim: You can optionally enforce the same workgroup-wide settings for all queries in a workgroup: query results location, expected bucket owner, encryption, and control of objects written to the results bucket.
question: Which settings can an Athena workgroup enforce on all its queries?

values.display: enforce the same workgroup-wide settings for all queries
query results location in Amazon S3, expected bucket owner, encryption

evidence.quote: You can optionally enforce the same workgroup-wide settings for all queries that run in the workgroup. These settings include query results location in Amazon S3, expected bucket owner, encryption, and control of objects written to the query results bucket.

claim: Athena lets you set per-query and per-workgroup data usage controls. It cancels queries that exceed the specified threshold, or activates an Amazon SNS alarm when a workgroup threshold is breached.
question: How can you limit how much data a team can scan with Athena?

values.display: Athena cancels queries when they exceed the specified threshold
activates an Amazon SNS alarm when a workgroup threshold is breached

evidence.quote: Create data usage controls – In Athena, you can configure per-query and per-workgroup data usage controls. Athena cancels queries when they exceed the specified threshold or activates an Amazon SNS alarm when a workgroup threshold is breached.

claim: Athena has two types of cost controls, a per-query limit and a per-workgroup limit. Each workgroup can have only one per-query limit and multiple per-workgroup limits.
question: How many per-query and per-workgroup data usage limits can a workgroup have?

values.display: only one per-query limit
multiple per-workgroup limits

evidence.quote: Athena allows you to set two types of cost controls: per-query limit and per-workgroup limit. For each workgroup, you can set only one per-query limit and multiple per-workgroup limits.

claim: The per-query control limit is the total amount of data scanned per query. If a query in the workgroup exceeds it, the query is canceled, and canceled queries are charged according to Athena pricing.
question: What happens to a query that exceeds the per-query data scanned limit, and is it billed?

values.display: If any query that runs in the workgroup exceeds the limit, it is canceled
Canceled queries are charged according to Amazon Athena pricing

evidence.quote: The per-query control limit specifies the total amount of data scanned per query. If any query that runs in the workgroup exceeds the limit, it is canceled. Canceled queries are charged according to Amazon Athena pricing.

claim: The default action when a query exceeds the per-query data scanned limit is to cancel the query, and this setting cannot be changed.
question: Can you change what Athena does when a query exceeds the per-query data limit?

values.display: The default action is to cancel the query
This setting cannot be changed

evidence.quote: The default action is to cancel the query if it exceeds the limit. This setting cannot be changed.

claim: Per-workgroup data usage alerts use CloudWatch alarms and apply to all queries in the workgroup. When a threshold is reached, Amazon SNS can email the users you specify, but queries are not automatically canceled.
question: Does a per-workgroup data usage threshold cancel queries?

values.display: implemented using Amazon CloudWatch alarms
Queries are not automatically canceled when a threshold is reached

evidence.quote: You can set multiple alert thresholds when queries running in a workgroup scan a specified amount of data within a specific period. Alerts are implemented using Amazon CloudWatch alarms and apply to all queries in the workgroup. When a threshold is reached, you can have Amazon SNS send an email to users that you specify. Queries are not automatically canceled when a threshold is reached.

claim: The workgroup-wide data usage control limit sets thresholds on hourly or daily aggregates of the data scanned by all queries in the workgroup. If it is exceeded, an action can send an Amazon SNS notification, invoke a Lambda function, or disable the workgroup.
question: What does the per-workgroup data usage control measure and what can it trigger?

values.display: thresholds on hourly or daily aggregates on data scanned
Disable the workgroup to stop any further queries from running

evidence.quote: The workgroup-wide query limit allows you to set multiple thresholds on hourly or daily aggregates on data scanned by queries running in the workgroup.
Disable the workgroup to stop any further queries from running.

claim: The per-query and per-workgroup limits are independent, and the specified action is taken whenever either limit is exceeded.
question: How do per-query and per-workgroup limits interact?

values.display: independent of each other
taken whenever either limit is exceeded

evidence.quote: The per-query and per-workgroup limits are independent of each other. A specified action is taken whenever either limit is exceeded.

claim: You can tag Athena workgroups with cost allocation tags, and the costs of running queries in the workgroup then appear in Cost and Usage Reports with that tag.
question: How do you allocate Athena query costs to a team?

values.display: tag workgroups with cost allocation tags
appear in your Cost and Usage Reports

evidence.quote: Use cost allocation tags – Use the Billing and Cost Management console to tag workgroups with cost allocation tags. The costs associated with running queries in the workgroup appear in your Cost and Usage Reports with the corresponding cost allocation tag.

claim: A workgroup can publish its query metrics to CloudWatch, where you can build dashboards and set thresholds and alarms, and Athena sends query state events to Amazon EventBridge in real time.
question: How do you monitor Athena queries per workgroup?

values.display: Publish the query metrics for your workgroup to CloudWatch
real-time notifications regarding the state of your queries

evidence.quote: Publish query metrics – Publish the query metrics for your workgroup to CloudWatch. In the Athena console, you can view query metrics for each workgroup. In CloudWatch, you can create custom dashboards, and set thresholds and alarms on these metrics.
Monitor query events – Use Amazon EventBridge to receive real-time notifications regarding the state of your queries.

claim: Each account has a primary workgroup. If you create no workgroups, all queries run in it by default. It cannot be deleted, and the default permissions allow all authenticated users access.
question: Where do Athena queries run if you create no workgroups?

values.display: Each account has a primary workgroup
The primary workgroup cannot be deleted

evidence.quote: Each account has a primary workgroup. By default, if you have not created any workgroups, all queries in your account run in the primary workgroup. The primary workgroup cannot be deleted. The default permissions allow all authenticated users access to this workgroup.

claim: Workgroups can be disabled. Disabling a workgroup prevents queries from running in it until you re-enable it.
question: What does disabling an Athena workgroup do?

values.display: Workgroups can be disabled
prevents queries from running in the workgroup until you re-enable

evidence.quote: Workgroups can be disabled. Disabling a workgroup prevents queries from running in the workgroup until you re-enable the workgroup.
